guard: a startMembershipFeed startup that rejects drains every connection it had already opened
why: The leak is invisible to the feed itself: the function rejects with the caller's own error either
way, and a suite that tears down with `finally { feed?.stop() }` sees `feed` as undefined on a
reject, so the connection it should have closed is never named. The named cell therefore grades the
BROKER's connection table through CONNZ rather than anything the feed reports about itself.
The sibling cell asserting the rejection text cannot grade this alone: it passes both before and
after the fix, which is exactly why the leak survived.
THE RECORD HAS TWO PUSH SITES AND THE MUTATION ABOVE GRADES ONE OF THEM. It reddens a cell that
counts the observer connection, pushed first, so it establishes the guarantee for conn A alone
while the guard claims EVERY connection. The conn B mutation below closes that. It was unkillable
until this suite gained a scenario that rejects with both connections already recorded: every
earlier scenario rejected at the credential source, which is awaited BEFORE conn B is pushed, so
at the moment of rejection the record held conn A alone and removing the conn B push changed
nothing any assertion could observe. A mutation whose target nothing observes does not go red, it
goes silent, and silence reads exactly like a guarantee that holds.

mutations.name: the transactional drain closes nothing
mutations.expectRed: conn A is drained when startup rejects - no orphaned observer connection on the broker
mutations.cell: conn A is drained when startup rejects - no orphaned observer connection on the broker
mutations.note: Keeps the handler, the record and the rethrow, and drains an empty slice: the reported behavior with the tree still compiling and every other cell green. The connection count on the broker stays one above the baseline for the rest of the run.

mutations.name: the conn B record is never made
mutations.expectRed: conn B is drained too when startup rejects after it was recorded - no orphaned rw connection on the broker
mutations.cell: conn B is drained too when startup rejects after it was recorded - no orphaned rw connection on the broker
mutations.note: The second push site. Conn B still dials and still works, it is simply absent from the rollback record, so a rejection below it leaves it open on the broker. Graded on the broker's connection table keyed by conn B's own connection name, because the conn A count passes whether or not conn B was drained.
